title: Margaret on whites stealing at the Savoy
summary: Mrs. JCH describes Goodman and others taking down the Savoy bands' music while musicians thought it cute.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Maybe Mrs. Higginbotham can tell us something about that.

I can tell you an awful lot about that. I used to go to the Savoy Ballroom every Sunday in my life when I was a youngster. I didn't miss a Sunday. He and Chick Webb, Sidney Catlett, Walter Johnson, Sammy Williams - we had two bands at the Savoy Ballroom, you know. I was young...you all weren't even born then. We had two bands at the Savoy Ballroom. Jay was in the Chick Webb band and then there was another band which I can't remember. I even told them. I said, 'These white musicians are not up here for nothing. They're up here for a reason. They're up here to steal everything they can get. Benny Goodman was one of them. 'Cause I met him, he sat at the table and drank
with me and everything. He wrote down everything these kids would write - would play.
How do you mean that? He wrote it down as they were playing?
He wrote down their music.
I know, but as they were playing?
That's right... Well, they thought it was great because a white man came up there to listen to them.
They weren't aware that he was taking...
No, they thought it was the greatest thing that the white man came to listen to them. You don't have to take my word. You can take all of my friends' words...
We were playing something that they couldn't catch up with.
But didn't they catch up with it? They caught up with it financially, though, didn't they? Didn't you feel anything about that?

I was married to him and I was out having a good time. But I told Walter Johnson - he was a drummer - you know, we always sat at a table together. I used to tell them, these white people are not up here for no good. They stole every thing, but they thought it was cute for a white man to be up there listening to them play, you know, they thought it was cute. When you know anything, Benny Goodman stole everything.
You said that Harry James was up there, and Tommy Dorsey.
All of them... sitting right there at the Savoy Ballroom.
And all the musicians felt that way. They thought it was a cute thing, huh?
I wouldn't call it cute. We just played and didn't give a darn and if you can catch up with it, that's up to you.

You see, I wasn't supposed to have no good sense. I was just about 22 or 23 years old. I wasn't supposed to know what it was all about. But I knew what they were doing. I used to tell Walter Johnson and Sidney Catlett and all of them that these white musicians ain't up here for no good, no good, and they stole everything! But they never could steal Jay's style, but they stole everything else. Even Chick Webb. Chick Webb and I were the best of friends. He used to say, "Why do they come up here?" Benny Goodman
What did Chick Webb say about that?
He died soon after.
Chick didn't give a darn. The only thing he wanted to do was get on that bandstand and play.
Now this was the feeling of most of the musicians?

I'll tell you, kids, /...The Negro they had (the sound) both to stand in the bottom and the stopper their hands and they let the white man take it away from them. Now I'm telling the truth, 'cause I was here and I was there, but they couldn't steal everything. They never could steal certain styles, but they could steal most styles.
